question: ADR-002 item 3 and PRD v2 Demo accounts leave timeZone's machine-checked shape open: what does the schema accept for the profile's timeZone?

options.label: booking-api@v1's room timeZone pattern
options.consequence: A string matching ^[A-Za-z_]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_+-]+)+$, the pattern booking-api@v1 already uses for a room's timeZone: an offset, an abbreviation, a bare city or an empty string fails the producer's replay; any IANA Area/Location name passes, so a third office needs no schema change. A name without a slash (UTC) fails, which no built-in account uses.

options.label: any non-empty string
options.consequence: The loosest check: Jakarta, WIB or +07:00 pass the replay, and the profile's zone and a room's zone could be the same kind of value in name only.

options.label: an enum of Asia/Jakarta and Europe/London
options.consequence: The tightest check, but a third office's zone becomes a schema change, and a consumer that switches exhaustively on the enum can break on it, which additive-only forbids.

why: ADR-002 item 7 compares a room's timeZone with the user's as names, so both contracts should accept the same kind of value; reusing the pattern booking-api@v1's schema already carries keeps them one shape without a shared code package. The enum would turn a new office into a schema change a consumer could break on, and a plain string lets non-IANA values through the producer's replay. The experiment shows the pattern rejects a number, an offset, a bare city, an abbreviation and an empty string, and that both demo zones resolve in Intl to their own names. A built-in account in UTC or another slash-less zone would have argued for a looser pattern.

question: Q-011: an optional timeZone under additive-only leaves a consumer nothing to fall back on, and ADR-002 lets the web app use no other zone; what does profile-api@v2 promise about timeZone being present?

options.label: optional in the schema, a guarantee that every 200 profile carries it
options.consequence: The schema keeps timeZone optional, so the pre-touch fixtures still validate (the additive-only condition). A guarantee says the producer sends it in every 200 profile; the built-in accounts are the only accounts (PRD v2 Users: no sign-up) and both their fixtures carry it with replay exact, so the producer's replay fails without it. A second guarantee says a consumer never puts another zone in its place (ADR-002 item 3): a profile without timeZone, which only a producer that predates this amendment serves, gets no time shown. Consumers type it as present and still meet its absence without guessing.

options.label: optional, with no presence promise
options.consequence: The smallest text, but consumers must treat absence as a normal answer for good, and since ADR-002 forbids a fallback zone the web app would carry a permanent no-times state no PRD v2 criterion allows (AC-2.1, AC-2.5).

options.label: required in the schema
options.consequence: Consumers get the presence from the schema itself, but the pre-touch me-ayu and me-budi fixtures fail it (experiment), so additive-only cannot claim it: a profile-api@v3 under lockstep (one endpoint, one shape), v2 deprecated in this run, a migration phase in every consumer node, and a breaking-amend stop.

chosen: optional in the schema, a guarantee that every 200 profile carries it
why: Q-011 asks the touch to state that the producer always sends timeZone for the built-in accounts or to weigh the gap in its classification. A guarantee closes the gap without breaking the version: the schema's optionality only keeps the pre-amendment shape valid, while the producer's obligation is stated and machine-checked, because the two built-in accounts are every account there is and their fixtures replay exactly. The no-substitute guarantee turns 'nothing to fall back on' into a defined consumer behavior that matches ADR-002 item 3 and its Consequences ('The web app shows no booking time until it has the profile'). That gap is real for a while: PRD v2 Team and delivery has backend and web ship separately, so the web app can meet a backend that has not yet shipped timeZone. Accounts created at runtime (sign-up), which no fixture could cover, would have pushed this to the required-field option and v3.

question: profile-api@v2's guarantees carry no ids, while hsdd-contract says each bullet under Guarantees / invariants opens G{n}:. Number them in this touch, which adds two?

options.label: number them G1 to G8 in their order
options.consequence: The six existing guarantees keep their text and meaning and gain ids, the two timeZone guarantees placed after the phone one. The backend, web and integration phase plans this run writes (H14, H16, H18) can cite one guarantee by id, as they can for auth-api@v1 and booking-api@v1. Nothing cites a profile-api@v2 guarantee by id today.

options.label: leave them unnumbered
options.consequence: The smallest diff, and the same form as profile-api@v1; the new timeZone guarantees are cited by quotation, and the skill's format rule stays unmet in a section this touch rewrites.

chosen: number them G1 to G8 in their order
why: Same reasoning as DEC-059 for auth-api@v1: the skill's format rule asks for ids so fixtures and phase gates can cite one guarantee, and the phase plans this segment writes will gate on the timeZone guarantees. A search of hsdd/spec, hsdd/verify, hsdd/management, hsdd/adr, the contracts, backend, web and e2e finds no citation of a profile-api@v2 guarantee by id. Ids are prefixes only, so the change is editorial and v2 stays. A citation of a guarantee by number would have argued for leaving them alone.

question: Classify the addition of timeZone (optional in the schema, promised present by G4, never substituted by G5, with the guarantees numbered) against profile-api@v2's additive-only rule, which keeps v2 only for an optional field that leaves the existing fixtures valid.

options.label: compatible: v2 stays, one dated Versioning entry
options.consequence: No new file, schema or fixture directory; status stays stable, phase_ids final, and produced_by and consumers unchanged until the new phases' confirm entries reach hsdd-reconcile. profile-api@v1 is untouched. No migration mode, no deprecation, no ADR affects handoff and no citation move, because no version is superseded. The shipped producer's exact replay and its account tests fail on the new me-ayu and me-budi until its time-zone phase ships, which is how a fixture change is meant to show.

options.label: breaking: draft profile-api@v3
options.consequence: A profile-api.v3.md with timeZone required, its own schema and fixtures, a lockstep migration note (one endpoint, one shape), v2 deprecated in this run while v1 still waits on Sync A, ADR-001 and ADR-002 affects handoffs, a migration phase in web and integration, and a breaking-amend stop on a stable contract.

chosen: compatible: v2 stays, one dated Versioning entry
why: The skill's additive-only row lets a change keep the version only if the version's existing fixtures still pass against the changed schema, and the contract's own Validation says an amendment adds its new optional field in the same edit. The experiment shows all five pre-touch fixtures validate against the amended schema, the live schema equals that optional candidate, and the same field made required would reject the pre-touch me-ayu and me-budi. No field is removed, retyped or repurposed. G4 adds a producer obligation and G5 a consumer rule that follows ADR-002 item 3; neither takes anything from a consumer that ignores unknown fields (G2), which is the class of the 2026-10-30 phone migration note. The ids are prefixes (DEC-064). A guarantee that needed timeZone required in the schema, or a consumer that rejects unknown fields, would have made it breaking and a stop.

question: S07's report lists reads outside its inputs (the backend's account data and tests, the web's profile decoder, earlier step records and booking-api@v1's schema). Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Keep the output
options.consequence: The profile-api@v2 touch stands; its routed items tell each phase plan which shipped test turns red until the field is served.

options.label: Rework without those reads
options.consequence: The step could not say which shipped tests the new fixtures break, and the phase plans would find out at their gates.

why: Whether an optional field is compatible for the shipped consumer depends on its decoder (decideProfile ignores unknown fields), and the producer-side effect on the exact replay depends on the account data; reading both is what the additive-only rule asks. All reads are inside the repository; none is out of bounds. A read outside the repository would have changed this.
